explain: C₂H₅ adds to CH₃CHO giving CH₃CH(OH)C₂H₅, butan-2-ol (2°).

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Wurtz reaction of tertiary alkyl halides with Na mainly gives what, instead of coupling?
explain: Bulky 3° halides undergo elimination, so Wurtz coupling fails.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Low reactivity of haloarenes to substitution
prompt: Why does chlorobenzene not undergo SN1 hydrolysis?
options: Cl⁻ is a very poor leaving group
explain: The phenyl cation has an sp² empty orbital in the ring plane, not conjugated with the π system, so it is unstable.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Low reactivity of haloarenes to substitution
prompt: Effect of a meta –NO₂ group on the rate of nucleophilic substitution of chlorobenzene?
explain: At meta, the negative charge of the intermediate is not delocalised onto the carbon bearing –NO₂, so there is little effect.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Low reactivity of haloarenes to substitution
prompt: 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene on warming with water gives?
explain: Three o/p –NO₂ groups activate the ring so strongly that water alone replaces Cl with OH, giving picric acid.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Low reactivity of haloarenes to substitution
prompt: Dipole moment of chlorobenzene compared with chloromethane?
explain: The sp² carbon is more electronegative and Cl donates electrons by resonance, so the dipole moment is lower.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Low reactivity of haloarenes to substitution
prompt: Order of reactivity towards aqueous NaOH (nucleophilic substitution)?
explain: More o/p –NO₂ groups give greater stabilisation of the intermediate. 2,4-dinitro reacts at 368 K, p-nitro at 443 K.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Low reactivity of haloarenes to substitution
prompt: Least reactive towards nucleophilic substitution (e.g. aq. NaOH) among these?
explain: Chlorobenzene has Cl on an sp² ring carbon. The others have halogen on an sp³ carbon.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Low reactivity of haloarenes to substitution
prompt: Which intermediate stabilisation explains faster substitution in p-nitrochlorobenzene?
explain: Para –NO₂ withdraws electrons by –M, so the negative charge of the carbanion intermediate is delocalised onto its oxygen.

subject: Chemistry
topic: EAS of haloarenes: o/p directing, deactivating
prompt: In nitration of chlorobenzene, the para isomer predominates over ortho mainly because of?
explain: Bulky Cl hinders ortho attack, and −I is also stronger at ortho, so para is the major product.

subject: Chemistry
topic: EAS of haloarenes: o/p directing, deactivating
prompt: Chlorobenzene reacts with CH₃COCl/anhyd. AlCl₃. The major product is?
explain: Friedel–Crafts acylation occurs at the para position (o/p director, ortho hindered).

subject: Chemistry
topic: EAS of haloarenes: o/p directing, deactivating
prompt: DDT is prepared by heating chlorobenzene with chloral in the presence of?
explain: Conc. H₂SO₄ catalyses EAS of two chlorobenzene molecules at para positions on chloral.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Polyhalogen uses & effects: CHCl3, CHI3, freons, DDT
prompt: Which freon is widely used as a refrigerant and aerosol propellant, and depletes the ozone layer?
explain: Freon-12 (CCl₂F₂) is a chlorofluorocarbon that releases Cl radicals in the stratosphere.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Polyhalogen uses & effects: CHCl3, CHI3, freons, DDT
prompt: Which species from CFCs in the stratosphere catalytically destroys ozone?
explain: UV splits C–Cl bond giving Cl•, which reacts with O₃ in a chain reaction.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Polyhalogen uses & effects: CHCl3, CHI3, freons, DDT
prompt: Iodoform was used earlier as an antiseptic because of which substance?
explain: The antiseptic action is due to the liberation of free iodine, not iodoform itself.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Polyhalogen uses & effects: CHCl3, CHI3, freons, DDT
prompt: DDT is chemically named?
explain: DDT = p,p'-dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane, an insecticide made from chlorobenzene and chloral.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Polyhalogen uses & effects: CHCl3, CHI3, freons, DDT
prompt: Why is DDT banned in many countries despite being an effective insecticide?
options: Reacts with water to form phosgene
explain: DDT is stable and non-biodegradable; it accumulates in fat tissues of living beings.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Polyhalogen uses & effects: CHCl3, CHI3, freons, DDT
prompt: Carbon tetrachloride is harmful mainly because its vapours cause which effect?
explain: CCl₄ vapours damage liver, and it contributes to ozone depletion.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which base best converts a 1° alkyl halide mainly into an alkene by E2?
explain: Bulky t-BuO⁻ is a poor nucleophile but a strong base, so SN2 is suppressed and elimination wins.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Total alkenes (including geometrical isomers) from 2-bromobutane on dehydrohalogenation?
explain: But-1-ene, cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene are formed.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: For E2 in a cyclohexyl halide, the leaving halogen must be in which position?
explain: Anti-periplanar (trans-diaxial) H and X are needed, so X must be axial.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which of these is NOT an ambident nucleophile?
explain: Cl⁻ is a single atom with only one attacking site; CN⁻, SCN⁻ and NO₂⁻ each have two.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: C₂H₅Br + alc. KCN, then complete acid hydrolysis of the product, gives
explain: KCN attacks through C, adding one carbon to give C₂H₅CN, which hydrolyses to propanoic acid.

subject: Chemistry
topic: EAS of haloarenes: o/p directing, deactivating
prompt: Correct order of rate of nitration: benzene, toluene, chlorobenzene?
explain: CH₃ activates (+I, hyperconjugation); Cl deactivates (−I > +M), so toluene > benzene > chlorobenzene.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Benzenediazonium chloride is converted to bromobenzene (Sandmeyer) using:
explain: Sandmeyer bromination uses Cu(I) bromide with HBr; the Cu powder/HBr variant is Gattermann.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: The Sandmeyer reaction of ArN₂⁺ with Cu(I) halide proceeds through which type of intermediate?
explain: Cu(I) transfers one electron to ArN₂⁺, giving Ar• with loss of N₂. Halogen transfer from Cu(II) halide follows.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Nitrobenzene on bromination with Br₂/FeBr₃ mainly gives:
explain: –NO₂ is a strongly deactivating meta-director, so electrophilic Br⁺ enters the meta position.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: 1-Bromobicyclo[2.2.1]heptane (bridgehead bromide) does not undergo SN2 mainly because?
options: Br⁻ is a poor leaving group
explain: The ring skeleton blocks backside attack at the bridgehead carbon, so no SN2 inversion is possible.

subject: Chemistry
topic: SN1 vs SN2: solvent, nucleophile, leaving group
prompt: In water, F⁻ is a poor nucleophile mainly because it is:
explain: Small F⁻ is tightly H-bonded by protic solvent, which lowers its nucleophilicity.

subject: Chemistry
topic: SN1 vs SN2: solvent, nucleophile, leaving group
prompt: Leaving-group ability of X⁻ generally correlates with which property?
explain: Weak bases (conjugate bases of strong acids) such as I⁻ and TsO⁻ leave easily.

subject: Chemistry
topic: SN1 vs SN2: solvent, nucleophile, leaving group
prompt: Which is the strongest nucleophile?
explain: Same attacking atom (O): nucleophilicity parallels basicity, and a negative charge increases it. Methoxide is the strongest base here.

subject: Chemistry
topic: SN1 vs SN2: solvent, nucleophile, leaving group
prompt: For SN1 hydrolysis of t-BuBr in aqueous ethanol, more water in the mixture:
explain: A higher-polarity protic medium stabilises the ionic transition state and the carbocation.

subject: Chemistry
topic: SN1 vs SN2: solvent, nucleophile, leaving group
prompt: A 2° alkyl bromide with CN⁻ (high concentration) in DMSO mainly reacts by:
explain: A strong nucleophile with a polar aprotic solvent favours SN2.

subject: Chemistry
topic: SN1 vs SN2: solvent, nucleophile, leaving group
prompt: CH₃Br does not react by SN1 mainly because:
explain: The methyl cation has no alkyl groups for hyperconjugation or +I stabilisation, so substitution goes by SN2.

subject: Chemistry
topic: SN1 vs SN2: solvent, nucleophile, leaving group
prompt: Aqueous AgNO₃ promotes SN1 of R–X because Ag⁺:
explain: Precipitation of AgX assists C–X ionisation, so it favours carbocation formation.

subject: Chemistry
topic: SN1 vs SN2: solvent, nucleophile, leaving group
prompt: In ethanol, RS⁻ is a stronger nucleophile than RO⁻ mainly because RS⁻ has:
explain: Large, polarisable S⁻ is less H-bonded by protic solvent, so it is a better nucleophile though a weaker base.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Order of ease of E1 dehydrohalogenation among alkyl halides of similar size is:
explain: E1 goes through a carbocation, and carbocation stability follows 3° > 2° > 1°.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which halide has no β-hydrogen and so cannot give an alkene directly by dehydrohalogenation?
explain: (CH₃)₃C–CH₂Br: the β-carbon is quaternary, so there is no β-H to remove.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: BrCH₂CH₂Br with one equivalent of alcoholic KOH mainly gives?
explain: One HBr is removed to give vinyl bromide. Excess base or NaNH₂ is needed to reach the alkyne.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Partial hydrolysis of an alkyl cyanide R–CN (controlled, H⁺/OH⁻, H₂O) gives:
explain: R–CN → R–CONH₂ (amide) → R–COOH on complete hydrolysis.

subject: Chemistry
prompt: Which is correct for the ambident NO₂⁻ ion in its nucleophilic attack?
options: N or O can attack the carbon
Attacks through N only with R–Cl
explain: Resonance places a lone pair on both N and O, so NO₂⁻ can attack through either atom.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Low reactivity of haloarenes to substitution
prompt: Effect of a para –CH₃ (electron-donating) group on SNAr rate of chlorobenzene with OH⁻?
options: Rate increases only at high pressure
explain: +I/+R groups destabilise the carbanion intermediate, so substitution becomes even harder.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Low reactivity of haloarenes to substitution
prompt: p-Nitrochlorobenzene with 15% NaOH at 443 K, then H⁺, gives mainly:
explain: –NO₂ at para activates SNAr, so Cl is replaced by OH, giving p-nitrophenol.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Polyhalogen uses & effects: CHCl3, CHI3, freons, DDT
prompt: Chloroform on warming with conc. HNO₃ gives which tear-gas compound?
explain: Nitration of CHCl₃ by conc. HNO₃ gives trichloronitromethane (chloropicrin), used as insecticide and tear gas.

subject: Chemistry
topic: Polyhalogen uses & effects: CHCl3, CHI3, freons, DDT
prompt: Which isomer of BHC (hexachlorocyclohexane) is the potent insecticide known as lindane?
explain: Only γ-BHC (lindane, gammexane) has strong insecticidal activity; it is about 99% pure γ-isomer.
